VIII. AN INDICATION OF WHAT THE OTHER INTERESTS AND CONSIDERATIONS
WERE TO AVOID SOME OR ALL OF THE PROBABLE AND ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS OF THE PROPOSED ACTION
A "Do-Nothing" alternative for Lincoln Highway would avoid some of the probable and adverse environmental effects of the proposed action. This alternative would not require the acquisition of privately owned lands nor use of lands subject to Section 4(f) of the Department of Transportation Act and would not disrupt any trees or indigenous vegetation. If a construction action or improvement is not undertaken or postponed pending further study, any divisive effects caused only by the roadway construction or reconstruction is eliminated.
Under the "To Improve" alternative, the alternates to relocate Lincoln Highway either to the north or south of its existing location, if feasible, would avoid some of the adverse environmental effects that the selected alternate would have upon the area adjacent to Lincoln Highway. An alternate either to the north or south would potentially lead to a reduction in the predicted traffic volumes in the Lincoln Highway area, which would result in a corresponding reduction in the predicted effects of noise and air pollution in the narrow band adjacent to Lincoln Highway. Any alternate to the north or south, however, would introduce high traffic volumes through areas where they do not presently exist. While the overall unavoidable polluting effects of the traffic would not be increased, they might be more objectionable in the areas where they are not now experienced in the same degree.
No other countervailing benefits can be foreseen for any of the alternates reviewed as opposed to the selected alternate. None of the other alignment alternates can be expected to avoid some or all of the probable and adverse environmental effects of the proposed action. At best, the probable and adverse effects of the selected alternate would only be transferred to an area that presently does not experience them in the same degree.
